The period is pre-released but the first FY27 outlook statement is a scheduled guidance event, and i0's H2 intake of about GBP26m against GBP44m a year earlier is derived across three of the company's own documents and has never been published; the July guide cut moved this name -29.6%, which sets the scale, and eMpulse plus the September insider buying are the only things pointing the other way.

Window is 10 Nov close to 11 Nov close on the hunter's timestamped amc check; H1 adjusted NI of 81.3m against a 115-140m FY guide leaves room to confirm at the upper end, the 62m HTC gain and 110m of RWA relief should put 30 Sep capital above SREP, and the disclosed short is covering from 6.06% to 4.33% - set against press-sourced write-down risk that is a buyer's diligence view and not a company number, on a name whose accounting days have run -44% and -55%.

Inflows are pre-released monthly and the single Equita bar already cut performance fees to 15m, so almost everything here is priced; the small residual is a flat-to-down Q3 for variable fees corroborated by Azimut's negative Q3 variable fees against an inflow-guide raise the market already models at 8bn.

A record pre-released quarter met by a bar raised three times in a month: NII consensus already sits at or above the top of the +15-18% guide (i2) and the aggregators carry a 0.60 interim that last year contained a 0.20 Mediobanca special (i3), against +5.2% over five sessions to above two of three targets.

i0 is the best-shaped finding on the day: the company's own 15%+ ROS guide implies USD 12-13m of H1 operating profit against a two-analyst, undated FY27 EBIT bar of about USD 18m, so the outlook line is more likely firmed or raised than cut, on a 138k-a-day stock that has given the whole September upgrade back and whose upgrades have paid +8.9%, +24.3% and +38.2%; Hubbell's heavy-industrial caution is the counterweight.

The Steam series (3,822 reviews, 114 concurrents) is a real independent read on an undisclosed number and this report is the first place the SEK 385m Cold Iron rights balance gets tested, but the stock is already -32% in 60 days, an impairment here is non-cash and the last clean-up day closed +26%, and the same quarter carries four releases against a weak comp - so the two legs very nearly cancel.

Genuinely two-sided: FY consensus of 662.6m sits at the very top of the 12% +/-2pp guide with no raise ad-hoc filed (i0, negative), against auto counterparties that printed well after Elmos last spoke (i1), an IFRS 2 liability that should flip to a gain and lift reported EBIT above operating (i4), and a 27% sector-wide de-rating with estimates unmoved on a name whose post-drawdown prints rallied +13.2% and +11.3% (i5).

The first full quarter of Sofar flips the revenue headline to double-digit growth on a retail-heavy 153k-a-day name (i0), but the margin has to clear a broker path of about 14.5% in H2 against the company's own 'approccio prudente', NFP/EBITDA is 2.7x against a 3.0x covenant with the buyback switched off since 16 Oct, Herbalife EMEA is still -4.9%, and the last three prints were sold 9-12%.

Window is 10 Nov close to 11 Nov close on the issuer's own after-close pattern; RFCF is tracking at or above the top of the 550-590m guide while the company's own page still carries 576m (i0), offset by revenue and EBITDAaL drifting under the consensus midpoint and an MSA dispute the Swisscom statement of 5 Nov already moved only -0.8%, with the take-private financing report putting a floor under a weak print.

The textbook pre-released case: the 21 Oct ad-hoc put out 9M revenue, EBITDA, orders and the raised margin guide and the stock took +12.1% that day, mid-term targets are reserved for the 3 Dec CMD, and all the release adds is a computable backlog and segment detail - a finding about a number the market has been told is worth about nothing, and the day's move will be mostly semicap beta.

An honest near-zero: the 9M adjusted result is arithmetic off VW's published 29 Oct Q3, the quarterly impairment is non-cash and was looked through twice this year, and the BGH ruling traded on 30 Sep - PAH3 has tracked VOW3 since, and nothing in the release is new.

Brazil MOP below the level the guide midpoint assumes and TTF at 100 against a 45 assumption both point at the lower half of 680-760m, but both are public series the 19% drawdown already carries; what is not published is the quarter itself (no Q3 consensus exists anywhere), where Nutrien's flat realised price on record Brazilian volumes and four straight Vara beats point up, with 4.04% disclosed short marginally covering as fuel.

Pandox's revenue-based leases over 48 Scandic hotels show RevPAR +6% and occupancy up two points against Scandic's own flat-occupancy guide, which is a good counterparty read - but the brokers raised targets on the same summer data in October, the stock is +25.8% in 60 days and above the four-month average target, the first Dalata pro-forma adds a +1% Ireland growth rate plus leverage, and this name sold its last three prints including an in-line one.

The quarter is pre-released in substance - the 12 Oct guide raise came 12 days after Q3 closed - and the bar was then lifted again by the 29 Oct Danske note that took the stock +7.1%, leaving a release that can only confirm an already-raised guide; the one open tail is the 2030 strategy the H1 report dates to Q4 2026 with no announced date, which is why abs sits above the 1.6% history.

The undisclosed Nscale 75MW CSA value, excluded from the Q2 backlog, first appears in Q3 order intake against a weak 1,043m comp, so the intake line should read strong and no number for it exists in the market; the Nscale counterparty strain is untransmitted and the Kvandal site is separately bank-financed, and NRK and Gallivare are already in the tape.

A depressed Q3-25 base (adj. EBITA 20.7 on Denmark close-outs and a Norvia restructuring with full effect from January 2026) against a quarter of public contract wins, corroborated by Svevia's Swedish-only PDF showing road O&M extra works up - a 202k-a-day name with one analyst and no quarterly consensus; the 3.9% margin guide needing about 5% in H2 is the real risk and keeps i2 negative.

Both load-bearing items already went out as MAR ad-hocs within six days of the print - the 9M figures and raised Adj. NI guide on 4 Nov, the dividend policy on 6 Nov - and the strategy belongs to the 16 Nov CMD outside the window; all that is left is how management explains an implied Q4 Adj. EBITDA of 76-276m against 456m a year earlier, and the independent evidence points to a real trough rather than a sandbag.
